sources.title: Threads
sources.locator: Threads; Where Threads Live; Start a Thread; Inside a Thread; Continue; Reference; Share; Export; Organize; Work Together; Artifacts
sources.finding: Threads have T-... URLs and open in web, CLI and all apps; they can run in an orb, on a runner or locally. Activity filters by time, status, author and project and searches with label: and other syntax. Messages sent while the agent works steer it; Cmd/Ctrl+Enter queues; Esc twice interrupts. Handoff starts a fresh thread with the relevant context; agents read threads by URL or @T- mention and search threads. Commits carry an Amp-Thread-ID trailer. Sharing is restricted, workspace or link; multiplayer contributors prompt, viewers read; admins open restricted threads through audited access. Export to Markdown, or full JSON for the creator. Labels, archive/unarchive, snooze, delete and per-thread cost are in the thread menu; snoozed threads awaiting approval reappear. Tagging a member turns on multiplayer. Artifacts are revisioned documents teammates and agents edit together.

sources.title: Orbs overview
sources.locator: Why Use an Orb; Orb Spawn Pacing; Terminal; Follow Along; Sync
sources.finding: Each orb thread gets a fresh isolated cloud environment with code, plugins and tools; work continues with the laptop closed; several tasks can run at once. A sleeping orb costs nothing and wakes with conversation, files and services in place. Each user gets a burst of 20 metered orbs, then one new orb every five minutes; later starts wait with an estimated wait instead of failing; higher limits via support. The Terminal tab is a shared tmux shell on the same working copy. Apps show the same threads and notify when a thread is ready.

sources.title: Orb sizes and costs
sources.locator: Available Sizes; Billing; When an Orb Pauses
sources.finding: Sizes a1.tiny to a1.3xlarge (1-16 CPUs, 2-44 GB, 60 GB disk) at $0.08-$2.13 per hour, billed per minute; a1.3xlarge only for Gigawatt and Enterprise. Self-hosted orbs are free on Hobby, Individual and Teams; Enterprise pays the standard price per minute. An orb pauses 5 minutes after agent work ends or 20 minutes after the last interaction, whichever is later; these are idle timeouts, not run limits. Archiving a thread pauses its orb immediately; left-running services pause with the orb and return when it wakes.

sources.title: Pricing (docs)
sources.locator: Amp Tiers; How Usage Is Charged; Enterprise; Notes
sources.finding: Hobby free; Individual Megawatt $20/month with 45,000 Amp-hosted orb minutes (Gigawatt price not rendered in the static page); Megawatt 50 $50/month with 2.5x included usage; Teams no extra charge, SAML/OIDC SSO, pooled credits; Enterprise custom, pooled credits only, no paid seats, spend limits, higher quotas. sources.title: Models & Subagents
sources.locator: Subagents; System Models; Custom Agents; Oracle, Librarian, Finder; Claude Fable with BYOK
sources.finding: Task and Read Thread subagents run the thread model in their own context; Amp uses them automatically or on request. sources.title: Multiplayer

sources.title: Automations & Webhooks
sources.locator: Automations; Manage; Run Quietly; Webhooks; Delivery Guarantees

sources.title: Amp Security Reference
sources.locator: Certifications; Infrastructure & Service Providers; Data Security; Thread Data; Orb Data; Prompt Injection Defenses; User Authentication; Audit Logging; Model Training; System Components; Client Security; Secret Redaction
sources.finding: Vendor states SOC 2 Type II and annual pentests; reports by request through the Security Trust Portal. Lists GCP (US, threads, user data and telemetry), model providers, e2b orb compute and other subprocessors; TypeSafe Jev suggests next actions. Client and server do not store, clone or index the entire codebase. Deleted threads are removed within 30 days; Enterprise threads remain with the workspace when users leave. Paused orbs stay encrypted until thread deletion. Thread storage preserves prompts, responses, tool calls and results as an audit trail; a data management API exposes analytics and thread data. SCIM deprovisions; admin access to restricted threads needs passkey re-authentication. Training needs explicit opt-in, workspace admin approval, never on Enterprise. Secret redaction is best-effort. Amp offers no self-hosted deployment.

sources.title: Workspaces | Amp Docs
sources.locator: Member tiers; Pay for Members
sources.finding: Team workspace admins can change a member's tier and set an optional base tier of Megawatt or Gigawatt for all members; service accounts never get a base tier seat and do not count toward its price.
